projects.title: ♟️ Automated Chessboard
projects.description: In our automated chess board capstone, I led the development team to create a shelf-ready product integrating hardware and software seamlessly. Using a Raspberry Pi-controlled CoreXY mechanism and Lichess API, we enabled games with online opponents and bots. Overcoming hardware issues with custom solutions, I helped ensure smooth communication between components and implemented essential features like automated moves and user-friendly interactions, delivering a fully functional product that blends physical and digital chess experiences. projects.title: Issue Tracker using NextJS
projects.description: My Issue Tracker application is a full-stack solution developed with Next.js, TypeScript, Google Authentication, OAuth, and Radix UI. It’s designed to streamline issue tracking by enabling users to categorize, assign, and monitor progress efficiently. The frontend ensures a responsive UI, while TypeScript enforces type safety across the application. The integration of Google Authentication and OAuth ensures secure user access, and Radix UI components maintain a seamless user experience. This project reflects my commitment to creating structured, scalable, and user-centric solutions.

projects.title: Multi Agent Path Finding
projects.description: Implemented Safe Interval Path Planning (SIPP), a faster algorithm than A* in dynamic path planning Studied multiple research papers and developed an algorithm byimplementing dynamic, safe intervals, which eliminated recalculatingpaths on every timestep, reducing the generated state spaceSuccessfully calculated optimal paths and the program ran 30%-40% faster than A* in general cases

projects.title: Affective Computing
projects.description: Generated artificial facial expressions based on gender, race and environment. Led a group of 3 to train the AI model producing appropriate Action Units (AUs). Collected wild and premade datasets from the web and trained the AI using Gaussian Mixture Model to separate the AU clusters. Verified the accuracy using K fold cross-validation. Generated 100 sensible facial expressions and classified them based on Plutchik’s Wheel of Emotions

projects.title: FTP Y-Modem Protocol
projects.description: Debugged and corrected the functionality of a multi-threaded socket-pair application.The thread had different real time priorities. Sender data was passed through a medium thread which corrupted, dropped and injected random characters upon receiving. Developed state chart and thread table to understand the program's flow. Implemented a CRC16 checker so receiver can request same block of 128 bytes if CRC's didn't match. Added dump glitches function to dump glitched characters(noise) stored in socket pair before the last byte was sent. Successfully verified the functionality of the terminal program by sending 100 files and received an A for the course

projects.title: FIQ & EIC Interrupts
projects.description: Assigned task was to strobe LED's on a STR730 micro controller using fast interrupts while the processor was busy calculating large Fib number. Read reference manual to initialize timer circuit within micro controller to periodically generate FIQ using Pulse Width Modulation. Adjusted pre-scale division and synced the fast interrupts to smoothly strobe LED's receiving a 90% on the project
